data.to:
Write down the measurement design so runs are defensible and affordable.

Cover:
- paired design: run the same forms through every dialect, compare within each item, use McNemar tests (a paired test for binary outcomes) — current practice, but not written down
- sample size: for a binary outcome the 95% confidence interval half-width is about 1 over the square root of n; n=100 gives about 10 percentage points, n=400 gives about 5; paired differences need far fewer samples
- model tiers: run the full dialect grid on cheap models and a reduced grid on 2 or 3 large models
- batch APIs cost half price
- gate visual dialects behind a cost check

Hard limit: 100 US dollars total for evaluation runs, paid out of pocket. notebooks/measurement.org holds earlier thinking; reconcile with it. The release skill (DB-8) follows this doc.

data.to:
Read .lattice/notes/design-decisions-2026-07-04.md first. It binds this task.

Write the measurement design doc the release skill (DB-8) and every run follows. Cover:

- the headline metric: per-model sensitivity score, defined as the paired accuracy drop against the canonical dialect over the frozen suite
- paired design: same forms through every dialect, within-item comparison, McNemar tests, bootstrap confidence intervals over items
- suite freezing: suite v1 fixes dialects, forms and seeds; scores always report per suite version
- sampling: one sample per (form, dialect, model); document the retirement of the old k=3, 4-expressions-per-sample, all-pass design and why scores break across that change
- sample size: confidence interval maths and a power argument for the paired design; concrete n per cell
- model grid, 4 tiers: cheap closed (full suite), 2 to 3 flagships (frozen core), open-weight via OpenRouter, reasoning-toggle pairs
- a worked budget sheet showing a full release run within 100 US dollars, stretch 150, using batch APIs at half price and gating visual dialects to cheap multimodal models first
- open questions section: prompt anchoring (parens examples in the system prompt; mixed brackets like [()] outperform (()); notation-neutral prompts make models default to parens) as a candidate ablation

Ground cost numbers in observed token usage from logs/ and notebooks/data-history, not guesses. Reconcile with notebooks/measurement.org. Put the doc where DB-8 can cite it (suggest docs/).

data.body: Open question from Valerie with rationale: the old 4-expressions-per-call all-pass design existed because (a) single marked/unmarked answers have a 50% guessing floor, (b) forms always simplify so large expressions reduce fast, (c) one expression per call wastes strong models' context and per-call overhead. DB-7 must decide whether bundling returns as a cost mode. Constraints if it does: per-expression scoring (never all-pass), call treated as a statistical cluster, identical bundling across dialects. Also record: suite v1 is a clean break; prior findings become pilot (v0) data.

Adversarial plan review (agent:claire-plan-reviewer-c). Spot-checks all pass.
- Token figures: EXACT against real logs. single WJ8d7dCM = 26,000 in / 28,366 out, n=100, sample lof_001 260 in / 228 out -- matches to the token. GPT-5.2 Y2VeJx = 17,226 in / 519,310 out / 514,657 reasoning, 30 samples -- exact. Sonnet 4.5 cdqvj = 128,162 total / 24,374 reasoning, 30 samples -- exact. The 'use these' figures are trustworthy; the implementer must not invent, and they won't need to.
- McNemar SE derivation: CONFIRMED CORRECT. Re-derived from the multinomial: S = (b-c)/n, Var(b-c) = n[p_b+p_c-(p_b-p_c)^2], so SE(S) = sqrt((b+c) - (b-c)^2/n)/n, approx sqrt(b+c)/n for small effects. The plan states this exactly (lines 197-204). The worked table checks out: n=100 & b+c=30 -> sqrt(30)/100 = 0.055 -> ~+/-11 pts; n=300 -> ~+/-6; n=500 -> ~+/-5. Internally consistent, and consistent with DB-5's exact-binomial McNemar + bootstrap.
- n vs cap: full suite 300-500 distinct forms (+/-5 to 6 on the drop) and core 100-150 (+/-9 to 11) is internally consistent with the SE table and the flagship-core role.
- Prompt anchoring open-question: CONFIRMED prompts.py keeps ()() = () and (()) = nothing.

FINDINGS:
1. (MEDIUM) Budget feasibility is asserted but not pre-validated. The plan defers the actual dialects x forms x tokens x price multiplication to the doc, but does not pin a single feasible configuration that sums to <= 100 USD. Flagship reasoning tokens (4k-20k/expression -- the plan's own 'heaviest risk') dominate: e.g. 3 flagships x ~600 core calls x 20k output x a flagship output price x 0.5 batch can exceed 100 USD on its own. AC requires the doc to sum to <=100/150; if the implementer discovers no feasible reasoning setting closes it, the AC is unsatisfiable. Fix: have the plan pin at least one concrete reasoning-setting/output-cap per flagship tier (and cite the matching low-reasoning log figure, e.g. Sonnet 4.5 ~4,270/sample) so a feasible point provably exists before the doc-writer starts.
2. (LOW) Cross-plan: your tier-4 reasoning-toggle sensitivity depends on the pipeline slicing the paired drop by reasoning setting, but DB-5's sensitivity.parquet currently groups by (model, dialect_id, suite_version) only -- no reasoning dimension (flagged on DB-5). Note the dependency so DB-8 doesn't cite a reasoning-toggle metric the pipeline can't produce.

No budget/CI/stat claim is unsupported; the stat spine is sound. Fixes are hardening, not rework. PASS WITH FIXES (pin a feasible flagship reasoning setting so the <=100 USD AC is demonstrably reachable; note the DB-5 reasoning-grouping dependency).

Review fixes applied: added a requirement that the budget section pin at least one concrete feasible flagship configuration (Sonnet 4.5, ~4,300 tokens/sample at 10k reasoning cap) proving a run closes under 100 USD, rather than merely asserting the cap is satisfiable. Noted the reasoning-toggle tier's dependency on DB-5's reasoning_setting column.

Implemented docs/measurement-design.md on branch spike/DB-7-measurement-doc (commit 5f51455, worktree agent-ab2da4f5dc0abcb36). 13 sections per the plan outline plus a data-source table. Every token figure traces to a named logs/*.eval (re-extracted and confirmed: single Sonnet 4 26k/28.4k; Sonnet 4.5 10k 4,272 tok/sample; Gemini 3 Pro 5,196 tok/expr; Opus 4.5 64k 80.4M anti-pattern); every price cited with source+date (Anthropic via claude-api ref 2026-06-24; Gemini 3 Flash and Qwen3/OpenRouter retrieved 2026-07-04). Budget arithmetic recomputed twice via a Python snippet pasted in-doc: pinned flagship config (Sonnet 4.5, 10k cap, batch) = 22.10 USD for a 6-dialect x 120-form core, and 100 USD buys 543 distinct forms (>>150 target); full baseline run 45.71 USD, stretch 98.92 USD. Includes McNemar SE table, n-per-dialect-per-tier table, v0->v1 break, bundling-pilot design (per-expression scoring, call as cluster, numeric pass criterion), open-questions section, DB-5 reasoning_setting dependency flagged, and the research-credit framing. Ready for a cold review against the plan's acceptance criteria.

Review (agent:claire-reviewer-db7), cold read as sceptical statistician against plan task_01KWQKYVS1C7JA2NHQT10MGY2B and rendering-architecture note. VERDICT: PASS. No implementation- or plan-level rework needed; no inline fixes required (found no typos or arithmetic slips to correct).

STATISTICS (all re-derived independently, all correct):
- McNemar SE(S)=sqrt((b+c)-(b-c)^2/n)/n is the exact plug-in SD(D)/sqrt(n) for D_i=X_i-Y_i in {-1,0,+1}; small-effect approx sqrt(b+c)/n = sqrt(r/n) checks out. Formula and approximation both sound.
- SE/half-width table (n=100/300/500 x r=0.1/0.3/0.5) reproduces to the quoted 1 dp in every one of the 9 cells. The prose read-offs (n=100,r=0.3 -> +/-11; 300 -> +/-6; 500 -> +/-5) and the 400-form/r=0.3 -> 5-6pt claim (I get 5.4) are correct.
- Unpaired baseline 1.96*0.5/sqrt(n): n=100 -> 9.8pp, n=400 -> 4.9pp. Correct; 'conservative worst case at p=0.5' is genuinely the max-variance point, so shown not just asserted.
- n-per-tier table is internally consistent (5x60=300, 5x100=500, 5x80=400; flagship 5x20=100, 5x30=150).
- Guessing-floor argument holds for the worst case: both dialects near chance -> equal accuracy -> S~0, correct reading. Bootstrap over distinct form strings + duplicate-form de-dup correctly addresses pseudo-replication from generate_form_string repeats.

BUDGET (recomputed from scratch in a separate snippet from the doc's stated inputs; all match):
- pc_batch 0.03069/call; flagship core 22.10 batch / 44.19 std; forms per $100 = 543 batch / 271 std. MATCH.
- Baseline lines t1 4.22, vis 2.16, t2 22.10, t3 11.20, t4on 5.66, t4off 0.37 -> total 45.71. MATCH.
- Stretch lines 5.28/5.09/27.62/39.39/14.00/7.08/0.46 -> 98.92. MATCH.
- Image sensitivity std->hires at 400 forms: 2.16 -> 4.07, delta 1.91. MATCH.
So the doc's US$22.10 core, US$45.71 baseline, US$98.92 stretch all reproduce exactly.

LOG SPOT-CHECKS (inspect_ai header.json stats.model_usage, main repo logs/):
- cdqvj (Sonnet 4.5): total_tokens 128162 over 30 samples = 4272/sample. Doc's cited figure CONFIRMED exact.
- Zj9C (Gemini 3 Pro): total_tokens 1870785 over 90 samples = 20786/sample, /4 = 5196/expr. Doc's cited figure CONFIRMED exact.
- (bonus) WJ8d single: 26000 in / 28366 out over 100 (284/call). Matches the 260/300 model used.

COMPLETENESS: all 13 plan sections present and mapped. Binding requirements all satisfied: pinned feasible flagship config (sec 9, 720 calls @22.10 with forms-per-$100 shown), DB-5 reasoning_setting dependency (sec 8 tier 4), v0->v1 clean break (sec 12, no v1 number exists to be mis-compared and every v0/V1.1 figure is labelled pilot), bundling pilot with numeric pass criterion (sec 10: cost -40pct AND accuracy within unbundled 95pct CI), all three open questions (sec 11), ablation lattice + payload-hash gate + coverage-adjusted contrasts (sec 7) consistent with the rendering-architecture note, research-credit framing (sec 13). Style is GOV.UK-clean: sentence-case headings, no Latin abbreviations in prose, the only bold is table-cell totals (tables exempt).

ADVISORY FINDINGS (minor; not blockers, do not require rework):
1. [medium] Sensitivity note (sec 9) commits to 'two assumptions dominate' = flagship reasoning + image tokens, but the OUT_REASON=5200 tok/expr proxy (Gemini 3 Pro) is load-bearing for the Qwen open-weight line (11.20) and the Gemini toggle-on line (5.66) = 16.86 of the 45.71 baseline (~37pct), applied cross-model with no stated range. The doc's own logs span 4270-20800 tok/sample, so a 3-4x miss on that proxy moves those lines materially (t3 alone -> ~45 at 20.8k/expr). The doc satisfies the plan's acceptance criterion (which scoped the note to flagship+image), so this is a recommended one-sentence addition, not a defect. Flagged because the plan itself listed the per-expression proxy as an adversarial risk.
2. [low] The paired design's tightness advantage is weakest exactly in the pure-guessing regime: guessing in both arms gives discordance r~0.5, the widest column of the SE table, so S~0 arrives with the widest CI. The conclusion ('no sensitivity to detect') is sound and the doc is not wrong, but a reader could infer the paired CI is uniformly tight.
3. [trivial] Batch-discount 50pct is sourced to the claude-api reference rather than the three provider batch docs (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) the plan named; OpenAI batch is not actually used in any grid line. Google batch 50pct is asserted via that same reference. The drift caveat covers this adequately.

None of these three changes any number or breaks any claim. Doc meets every acceptance criterion. Moving to done.
